full_judgment:
Fazle Munim, C.J:- Since I have dissented from the conclusions reached by the majority of the learned Judges, I have intended to give a separate judgment which is as follows. This appeal arises from judgment and order dated 11-9-85 passed by a Single Judge of the High Court Division Dhaka (Sultan Hossain Khan, J:) affirming in revision the decree passed concurrently by the Courts below. 

 a) For a decree be passed declaring that the seniority list in respect of the service of the plaintiffs and others concerned made on the basis of the merit list prepared on the results of test examination and interview held in recruitment of the plaintiffs and others of their group (i.e, Group-IV named Jr. Accounts Supervisor) and published vide Letter No. DACGF/SENIORITY/PIN/84/38 dated 5th January, 1984 is correct, legal and binding on all concerned and the seniority list now prepared In violation and contravention of the provisions laid down in Article 18 (a) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation, 1979 and published vide letter No. DACCF/SENIORITY/84/3191 dated 18-10-84 or made hereafter is and will be illegal, void, inoperative and without any binding force and hence any promotion or benefit, if given on the basis of the seniority list published vide DACGFI SENIORITY/ 84/ 3191 dated 18-10-84 or any other list prepared hereafter in respect of the personal of the service group of the plaintiffs (Group-IV named Jr. Accounts Supervisor) the same shall be illegal, void, inoperative and without any binding force in law. 

 b) For a decree and order restraining the defendants from changing or altering the seniority list prepared and published vide letter No. DACGF/SENIORITY/FIN/84/38 dated 5-1-84 on the basis thee of (i.e. the merit list) and from giving effect to the Seniority list prepared and published vide letter No. DACGF/SENIORITY/84/3191 dated 18-10-85 or any other seniority list prepared and published in contravention or violation of the provisions and spirit of Article 18(a) of Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulation, 1979. 

 c) For a decree for full costs of the suit against the defendants and in favour of the plaintiffs. 

 d) For a decree for such other relief or reliefs to which the plaintiffs may be entitled under the law and equity." 

 5. Respondents contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and barred by estoppel, waiver and acquiescence, declaration if granted, would affect the accrued and vested legal rights of third parties. Trial Court decreed the suit declaring that the seniority list which was prepared according to merit list on 5th January 1984 was legal and binding, whereas the seniority list made on 18th October 1984 was in violation of Regulation 18(a) of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employee (Service) Regulations, 1979 and was, therefore, illegal, void and without any binding force. 

 6. On appeal, being Title Appeal No. 146 of 1985, trial Court's judgment and decree were affirmed by the learned District Judge. Appellant Corporation preferred an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court Division, being Civil Revision No. 506 of 1986., The learned Judge of the High Court Division discharged the Rule on finding that respondents .being appointed under Ordinance XIX of 1977, the terms and conditions including seniority in service will be guided by the aforesaid Regulations which were published for the first time on 28th December 1979 and in determining their seniority Regulation 18 (a) shall apply, there being no question of retrospective operation of the service Regulations that respondents were new entrants as contemplated in Regulation 18, as they were appointed after the promulgation of the Ordinance on 9th June 1977, and according to section 31 (d) of the Ordinance No. XIX of 1977 existing employees would be those whose services were transferred to the Corporation on 9th June 1977. The learned Judge held that Regulation 19 applied for "existing employees" and the seniority of respondents were governed by Regulation 18(a). 

 24. Both the trial Court and the lower Appellate Court concurrently found that the respondents are 'new entrants' and not 'existing employees'; and as such, their seniority would be governed by rule 18(a). On this finding, the impugned Seniority list dated 28' October 1984 was declared violative of the Regulations and the suit was decreed. The reason given for this finding is that though the respondents had been appointed earlier then the Regulations, yet when both the appointment of the respondents and the Regulations were made under the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance, 1977, the classification of employees of the Corporation into existing employees and new entrants as indicated and contemplated in the said ordinance should be followed and that according to this ordinance, the respondents fall within the classification of 'new entrants'. The learned Single Judge of  the High Court Division on a revisional application under section 115 of the Civil P.C. did not find any error in the decision of the appellate Court and as such refused to interfere therewith. 

 25. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate for the appellant, has seriously challenged the concurrent decision of all the Courts below as referred to above and has contended that the provisions of both the Biman Ordinance of 1977 and the Regulations of 1979 have been misconstrued and that the impugned decision in palpably erroneous, The learned Advocate has explained that the earlier Seniority list was prepared on erroneous view of law and in correct information’s about facts. The learned Advocate has argued that the Regulations, to be precise, rule 18(a), have not been given any retrospective operations, hut they are prospective in operation and when the respondents were appointed before the coming into force of the Regulations, which determine seniority and other terms and conditions of services of the Corporation's employees, their seniority must be governed under rule 18(a) of the Regulations treating them as existing employees. Another contention of the learned Advocate is that the suit itself is not maintainable in that the necessary parties, such a those employees whose seniority will be affected in case the suit is decreed, were not impleaded in the suit. In support of this contention the learned Advocate has referred to a decision of the Privy Council in the case of Nava Kumar Vs. Radhashyam. AIR 1931 (PC) 229 and another decision of the Federal Court in the case of United Provinces Vs. Atiqa Begum, AIR 1984 PC 16. 

 The Ordinance did not itself lay down the terms and conditions of service. There is no dispute that if the respondents are 'new entrants', as referred to in rule 18(a) of the Regulations, then the decree passed in their favour by the Courts below is correct. But if they "are existing employees' as referred to in rule 19(i)(a) of the Regulations, the decree is wrong. Rules IS and 19 of the Regulations are quoted below: 

 32. In the result, the impugned Seniority list prepared by the appellant on 18 October. 1984 is found prepared on correct interpretation of the Regulation. The impugned decree passed in the suit is therefore set aside and the suit is dismissed. The appeal is allowed. No order as to costs. 

 By the majority decision, the impugned decree is set aside and the suit is dismissed. The appeal is allowed. No order as to costs.
